question: Should every authoritative repair apply and post-flight mutation fail closed unless its trusted review authorization still matches the exact target, covering-PR, review-activity, and required-check state at the request boundary?
rationale: The implementation mechanics are well supported, but this deliberately changes the live security-versus-availability boundary and the operational treatment of legacy or incomplete authorization state.

options.title: Accept fail-closed rollout
options.body: Merge after an exact-current-head canary demonstrates both stale-state rejection and successful unchanged long-running repair publication.

options.title: Narrow guarded operations
options.body: Limit the new authorization boundary to the highest-risk merge and close operations before expanding it to other repair writes.

options.title: Pause broader enforcement
options.body: Retain the merged review-activity protection from https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/pull/557 without rolling out the additional request-boundary guards yet.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed rollout
recommendation.body: Merge after an exact-current-head canary demonstrates both stale-state rejection and successful unchanged long-running repair publication.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged precursor and current implementation history and are best positioned to explain the intended rollout and canary behavior.
